newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen raises petrol prices by over 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Yemen raises petrol prices by over 30 percent.

text.p: Yemen's oil ministry on Tuesday raised the price of petrol and kerosene, a move which in the past has sparked riots and protests.
A statement issued by the oil ministry and obtained by Reuters said the new prices came into effect at midday (0900 GMT) on Tuesday.
The ministry raised the price of petrol over 31 percent to 25 rials ($0.2) a litre from 19 rials and lifted the price of kerosene to 13 rials a litre from seven.
Fuel oil used at power stations and cement factories was raised to 11 rials from seven a litre, while diesel remains at six rials a litre.
Since late Monday long queues of cars have built up in front of petrol stations in the capital Sanaa and some other cities.

Residents said some petrol stations had closed ahead of the increase so that they could sell their petrol stocks at the higher price. They said queues also formed as motorists, expecting the hike, tried to take advantage of the cheaper, old price.
When Yemen increased the price of petrol to 19 rials from 12 in January 1996, Yemeni farmers and students took to the streets and blocked a major Sanaa-Aden highway in protest.
In 1995, riots erupted in the southern port city of Aden over the doubling of petrol prices.

Yemen, a small independent oil producer, began raising the price of petrol in March 1995 as part of the implementation of economic reforms agreed with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund. ($1=125 rials)
